name: Autosomal Recessive Spastic Paraplegia Type 24

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for SPG24

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the DDHD2 gene
MRI showing mild corticospinal tract abnormalities or normal imaging
Exclusion of other causes of spastic paraplegia by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity with confirmed biallelic pathogenic variants in DDHD2 gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other hereditary spastic paraplegias.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and infectious causes
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord may show mild corticospinal tract signal changes or be normal
other: Electromyography may show mild peripheral neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: SPG7 often presents with cerebellar ataxia and optic atrophy more frequently
SPG7 caused by mutations in the SPG7 gene
Adrenal insufficiency and elevated very long chain fatty acids
Progressive spastic paraparesis with peripheral neuropathy

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity and weakness
Presence of seizures or optic atrophy
references: Harding AE. Hereditary spastic paraplegias. Semin Neurol. 1993;13(4):333-342.
Tesson C, et al. DDHD2 mutations cause a recessive form of complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia. Am J Hum Genet. 2012;91(6):1073-1081.
